title: ITR Filing 2026: Retaining Digital Tax Documents Securely
description: While ITR filing is largely paperless, it is crucial to securely retain all relevant digital tax documents. These digital records are essential for responding.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to keep physical copies of tax documents?
faq.a: No, it is generally not mandatory to keep physical copies. The Income Tax Department accepts digital documents as valid proof for verification and assessment purposes.

faq.q: How long should I retain my digital tax records?
faq.a: It is advisable to retain most tax documents for at least 6 years from the end of the relevant assessment year. For specific cases like undisclosed foreign income, this period can extend up to 16 years.

faq.q: What happens if I lose my digital tax documents?
faq.a: Losing documents can complicate responding to tax notices. While some documents like Form 26AS and AIS can be re-downloaded from the Income Tax portal, others like investment proofs or rent receipts might be harder to retrieve, potentially leading to penalties if you cannot substantiate your claims.

faq.q: Can I use any cloud storage for my tax documents?
faq.a: Yes, you can use reputable cloud storage services like Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox. Ensure you use strong passwords and enable two-factor authentication for enhanced security.

faq.q: Is Form 16 sufficient for income proof?
faq.a: While Form 16 is crucial for salaried individuals, it's not always sufficient on its own. You should also retain Form 26AS, AIS/TIS, and bank statements to provide a comprehensive view of your income and tax deductions.

faq.q: What if I receive a notice years after filing my ITR?
faq.a: Tax authorities can issue notices for past assessment years within the prescribed retention periods. Having well-organised digital records allows you to quickly retrieve the necessary documents to respond accurately and avoid potential issues.

faq.q: Should NRIs also follow these digital record-keeping practices?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) filing ITR in India must also maintain digital records of their Indian income, TDS certificates, and any other relevant financial documents to ensure compliance and respond to any tax queries.
